batchName: Empire: The Five Good Emperors (AD 96-192) - Hard Batch 1

questions.question: When Trajan entered Rome in 99, how did he handle the customary cash gifts?
options: Gave equal sums to the people and the troops
Doubled the troops' gift and gave nothing to the people
Gave gifts to senators and no one else
Paid the troops entirely in Dacian gold
Cancelled all gifts to save money for war
Gave cash to the people but halved the troops' gift
questions.explanation: Trajan entered Rome with notable modesty, giving cash to the common people while halving the gift to the troops. He made a show of respecting the Senate.
questions.sourceQuote: He gave cash to the common people, though he halved the customary gift to the troops.

questions.question: Once Trajan held power, what happened to the Praetorian commander who had defied Nerva?
options: He was exiled to a small Aegean island
He was pardoned and kept his command
He killed himself before he could be seized
He was promoted to govern the new Dacia
Trajan summoned him and had him executed
He was made consul alongside Trajan
questions.explanation: Trajan summoned the Guard commander and had him put to death. Some historians see Trajan's accession as less an orderly succession than a successful coup.
questions.sourceQuote: He first summoned the Guard commander who had defied Nerva and had him put to death.

questions.question: How did the Romans locate the Dacian royal treasure?
options: Engineers found it while building the Danube bridge
Cavalry seized it alongside the fleeing king
A captured nobleman revealed it lay under a diverted river
It was dug up beneath the battlefield of Tapae
Miners found it in a shaft near Sarmizegetusa
The king's widow handed it over to save her life
questions.explanation: A captured nobleman revealed the treasure buried beneath a temporarily diverted river. One modern estimate puts it at about 165,500 kg of gold and 330,000 kg of silver.
questions.sourceQuote: A captured nobleman revealed that the royal treasure had been buried beneath a temporarily diverted river.

questions.question: When Marcus Aurelius's own son succeeded him in 180, how did a historian who lived through it describe the change?
options: From the bright noon of empire to its long dusk
From the rule of the best to the rule of the worst
From a reign of virtue to a tyranny of vice
From a kingdom of gold to one of iron and rust
From an age of philosophers to one of soldiers
From a city of marble to a city of mud
questions.explanation: The son's succession broke the run of adopted heirs, and a contemporary saw it as a fall from gold to iron and rust. Commodus ruled until 192.
questions.sourceQuote: A historian who lived through it wrote that Rome now fell 'from a kingdom of gold to one of iron and rust'.

questions.question: Which desert fortress city did Trajan fail to capture as his Parthian campaign unravelled?
options: Petra
Edessa
Palmyra
Hatra
Dura-Europos
Nisibis
questions.explanation: Trajan's failure at Hatra came amid revolts across Mesopotamia and Jewish uprisings in Egypt, Cyprus and Cyrene. His health then collapsed.
questions.sourceQuote: Trajan failed to take Hatra, a desert fortress city, and his health collapsed.

questions.question: Besides respecting their privileges, how did Antoninus win over the resentful senators?
options: By granting the Senate the right to elect emperors
By doubling senators' payments from the treasury
By promising to retake Trajan's eastern lands
By executing Hadrian's Praetorian commander
By moving the court from Tivoli back to Rome
By cancelling death sentences from Hadrian's last days
questions.explanation: Antoninus cancelled death sentences passed at the end of Hadrian's reign and respected senatorial privileges. Hadrian had died at Baiae on 10 July 138.
questions.sourceQuote: He won them over by respecting their privileges and cancelling death sentences passed in Hadrian's last days.

questions.question: Which of Trajan's newest conquests did Hadrian give up? (select all that apply)
options: Parts of Dacia, handed to a neighbouring people
Armenia, left to Parthian influence
Mesopotamia, abandoned as too costly to defend
The province of Britain, south of the Wall
Judaea, returned to a client king
The Rhine lands, ceded to Germanic tribes
questions.explanation: Hadrian abandoned Mesopotamia, let Armenia return to Parthian influence and handed parts of Dacia to a neighbouring people. Ancient writers blamed jealousy of Trajan; modern historians see a realistic retreat.
questions.sourceQuote: Mesopotamia was abandoned as too costly and distant to defend, Armenia returned to Parthian influence, and parts of Dacia were handed to a neighbouring people.

questions.question: Which factors do modern scholars think probably did most to provoke the Jewish revolt under Hadrian? (select all that apply)
options: A new tax to pay for Hadrian's Wall
Plague brought back from Parthia
Hopes of a messiah to rebuild the Temple
A Roman ban on circumcision
Heavy-handed Roman government
Quarrels over land
questions.explanation: A later tradition blamed a ban on circumcision, but modern scholars doubt it. Harsh government, land disputes and messianic hopes probably mattered more.
questions.sourceQuote: Heavy-handed government, quarrels over land and hopes of a messiah who would rebuild the Temple probably mattered more.

questions.question: Which emperor did a great 19th-century German scholar accuse of an 'insatiable lust for conquest'?
options: Nerva
Antoninus Pius
Trajan
Lucius Verus
Marcus Aurelius
Hadrian
questions.explanation: Though ancient writers adored Trajan, the German scholar condemned his conquests. The 18th-century English historian also doubted Trajan's warlike reign.
questions.sourceQuote: The same English historian doubted Trajan's warlike reign, and a great 19th-century German scholar spoke of his 'insatiable lust for conquest'.

questions.question: Which of these projects in or near Rome did Hadrian carry out? (select all that apply)
options: Raised a spiral victory column
Finished the domed Pantheon
Added libraries and a market to a forum
Built Rome's largest forum
Built a sprawling villa at Tivoli
Rebuilt the Circus Maximus in stone
questions.explanation: Hadrian finished the Pantheon in its familiar domed form and built a villa at Tivoli, east of Rome. The Circus Maximus, the great forum and the Column were all Trajan's work.
questions.sourceQuote: In Rome he finished the Pantheon in its familiar domed form and built a sprawling villa at Tivoli, in the hills east of the city.
